mutants.expected_detection: Evaluator directly compares submitted trojan_present boolean against ground truth (true) and fails the submission since it is falsely reported as false despite suspect_nets, trigger_condition, and affected_outputs all still describing the real Trojan.

Evaluator compares trigger_condition.address against ground truth '011' (and cross-validates via iverilog/vvp replay against decoder_netlist.v). This mutant reports address '010' instead, which does not trigger the dual bank0_we/bank2_we assertion when replayed, so SR2 (and consequently SR3) fails.

Evaluator performs set-equality check between submitted affected_outputs and ground-truth {bank0_we, bank2_we}, and/or cross-validates via simulation replay at addr=011/write_en=1 against decoder_netlist.v; this mutant reports affected_outputs as [bank1_we, bank2_we], which fails both the set-equality check (missing true positive bank0_we, spurious inclusion of bank1_we) and simulation replay (bank1_we never asserts at addr=011).

Evaluator cross-checks suspect_nets entries against the structural netlist to confirm the reported gate_instance/net actually drives bank2_we via the minterm3 tap. Here the suspect_nets list only names benign, unrelated decoder gates (u_minterm3, u_sel2_we) with role 'trigger'/'payload' and omits the true alias gates g_alias_tap_and/g_alias_or2 and their nets minterm3_tap_and/bank2_we_alias_tap entirely, so structural/behavioral matching against decoder_netlist.v fails to find the actual bridging instance, violating SR4 even though SR1-SR3 fields remain nominally correct.

Exhaustive simulation replay via testbench_harness.v against decoder_netlist.v shows that at address 001 (write_en=1) only bank1_we asserts (one-hot, no anomaly), contradicting the submission's false claim that bank1_we and bank3_we both assert at addr=001, so cross-checking suspect_nets/affected_outputs/evidence against exhaustive ground truth for the 7 non-Trojan addresses (SR5) flags this as a false positive.
FR1 must reject a syntactically malformed JSON submission.

Evaluator schema/field validation should detect that trigger_condition.address is '11' (a 2-character string) instead of the required 3-character binary string '011', and/or that design_under_test does not equal the exact required literal 'decoder_netlist.v', causing FR2 structural validation to fail.

Schema/content validator for FR3 should reject this submission because affected_outputs contains only a single entry ('bank2_we') despite trojan_present being true, violating the FR3 requirement that affected_outputs must contain at least two distinct entries when trojan_present is true. This also causes SR3 set-equality checks to fail since bank0_we is missing from the set.

Evaluator should detect that the submission's suspect_nets/evidence now make a blanket claim of anomalous behavior across all addresses (not scoped to address 011), violating FR4's requirement that the reported anomaly be scoped to a single specific address. Cross-checking suspect_nets roles against trigger_condition.address and the exhaustive simulation ground truth should reveal that the submission asserts the alias gates affect every address rather than only 011, and/or lists benign per-address decode gates (u_minterm0..u_minterm2, u_sel0_we..u_sel2_we) as trigger/payload, implying multi-address impact inconsistent with the single-address scoping FR4 mandates.
